Scathing

/SKAY-thing/ - rhymes with bathing · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Scathing means sharp, critical, hurtful.

The coach's halftime verdict was scathing enough that even the seniors studied their cleats like freshmen.

Worked Example

The retiring ambassador's memoir devoted one scathing chapter to her own ministry — promotions traded like baseball cards, cables unread for months — and the ministry, in reply, confirmed every page by demanding it be cut.

Scathing is criticism that leaves a mark — the word descends from an old verb for injuring, and the wound is the point. It is harsher than cutting and colder than an outburst: a scathing review is composed, aimed, and meant to scar. This unit's vituperate is louder and cruder; a scathing attack needs no shouting.

How Scathing Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

withering

withering: scorn that makes its target shrivel on the spot

cutting

cutting: sharp enough to wound in a single stroke

Antonyms

complimentary

complimentary: offering praise instead of blood

kindly

kindly: gentle and well-meaning in tone

How Strong Is It? — cutting → scathing → savage

cutting vs. scathing

cutting vs. scathing: Cutting is milder than scathing — one sharp stroke, quickly over.

savage vs. scathing

savage vs. scathing: Savage is fiercer than scathing: a scathing review is a scalpel with intent, while a savage one stops pretending to be surgery.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — scath

Root — scath: to harm, to injure (Old Norse skatha)

Suffix — -ing

Suffix — -ing: adjective ending (present participle)

Put it together

Put it together: Scath- (to harm — Old Norse skatha) + -ing = harming as it goes. English once used scathe as an everyday verb for injury; the participle survived as an adjective for words that do the injuring now that fists are out of fashion.

Use the root in a new word: unscathed

Use the root in a new word: unscathed: The cat walked out of the collapsed shed unscathed — not a whisker harmed.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / journalistic

Scathing is for criticism engineered to wound — reviews, reports, verdicts. Cutting fits one remark; withering fits a look or a put-down that shrivels; scathing sustains the attack for paragraphs. In this unit, upbraid is the act of scolding and vituperate the torrent of abuse — scathing describes the blade's edge itself.
